## Overview and complete interface

This module matches the original module's non-drainage six-class biomass
classification, while keeping its own module/output identity and stricter input
and overwrite safeguards. There is no drainage input or refinement. Biomass
replaces basal area and stem density in an adaptation of Hart et al. (2019),
Table 1 and section 2.4; equivalence is not ecological validation.

The shared reference below includes rules, parameter defaults, scheduling,
exports, migration and examples, avoiding conflicting copies of the interface.

```{r shared-reference, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat(readLines("README.md", warn = FALSE)[-1L], sep = "\n")
```

## Standalone example

Production inputs must be supplied explicitly; this example deliberately
constructs synthetic inputs instead of enabling a module demo mode.

```{r external-helper, eval=FALSE}
source("R/classifyHartJohnstoneForest.R")
source("R/hartJohnstoneDemoInputs.R")
exampleInputs <- hartJohnstoneDemoInputs()
forestClasses <- classifyHartJohnstoneForest(
  exampleInputs$cohortData, exampleInputs$pixelGroupMap,
  jackPineSp = c("Pinu_ban"), larchSp = c("Lari"), spruceSp = c("Pice"))
stopifnot(names(forestClasses) == "standtype")
# Optional explicit export, separate from classification:
source("R/writeHartJohnstoneForestMap.R")
writeHartJohnstoneForestMap(forestClasses, outputDirectory, simulationTime = 0)
```
